{{short description|German physicist}}
'''Gottfried Landwehr''' (22 August 1929 &ndash; 24 January 2013) was a [[:Category:German physicists|German physicist]].
{{Infobox scientist
|birth_date = {{Birth date|1929|8|22|}}
|birth_place = [[Osnabrück]]
|death_date = {{death date and age|df=yes|2013|1|24|1929|8|22}}

Landwehr was born in [[Osnabrück]] and studied physics in [[Karlsruhe]]. After that, he worked at the [[Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt]] in [[Braunschweig]]. He was one of the founders of the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]] in [[Stuttgart]] (1955) and headed the branch office in France until 1983. From 1968 to 1999 he was a professor for experimental physics in [[Würzburg]].  [[Klaus von Klitzing]] who is known for the discovery of the [[quantum Hall effect|integer quantum Hall Effect]] in 1980 ([[Nobel Prize]] 1985) was one of his students. 
On the initiative of Gottfried Landwehr the well known Centre for semiconductor physics was founded at the [[Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg]]. He is also associated with the founding of the chair of applied physics and the department of experimental physics V (biophysics).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mainpost.de/regional/wuerzburg/Physikprofessor-Gottfried-Landwehr-starb-mit-83-Jahren;art735,7275893 |title=Professor Gottfried Landwehr passed away at the age of 83 |work=[[Main-Post]] |date=1 February 2013 |access-date=1 February 2013 |archive-date=29 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129134144/https://www.mainpost.de/regional/wuerzburg/Physikprofessor-Gottfried-Landwehr-starb-mit-83-Jahren;art735,7275893 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Online condolence book ==
Landwehr died, aged 83, in [[Würzburg]].  The faculty decided to provide an [https://web.archive.org/web/20150613152101/http://www.physik.uni-wuerzburg.de/aktuelles/kondolenzbuch/ online condolence book] for the first time in its history.
